darkraimega.description: It can lull people to sleep and make them dream. It is active during nights of a new moon.

victini.description: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being’s entire body will be overflowing with power.

snivy.description: The leaf on Snivy’s tail generates energy when exposed to sunlight, making Snivy swifter and adding an edge to its moves.

servine.description: It runs low to the ground, weaving through the grass, then mercilessly pummels its target by whipping them with its vines.

serperior.description: It generates energy from sunlight, then amplifies that energy dozens of times within its long body.

tepig.description: It’s more nimble than it looks, and it uses its speed to confound its enemies. It rapidly launches fireballs from both nostrils.

pignite.description: When Pignite enters battle, its body temperature rapidly soars until Pignite itself is engulfed by a scorching fireball.

emboar.description: The flames blazing deep inside Emboar’s chest erupt vigorously from its chin, forming a beard of fire.

oshawott.description: It wields the scalchop on its stomach like a knife, blocking the moves of its enemies before slashing back at them in swift retaliation.

dewott.description: It’s said that people modeled swordplay after the way Dewott’s movements flow like water while it’s wielding its two scalchops.

samurott.description: A master of a sword-drawing art called iaijutsu, Samurott settles its battles with a single swing of either large sword sheathed in its foreleg armor.

patrat.description: Extremely cautious, one of them will always be on the lookout, but it won’t notice a foe coming from behind.

watchog.description: When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.

lillipup.description: This Pokémon is courageous but also cautious. It uses the soft fur covering its face to collect information about its surroundings.

herdier.description: Herdier is a very smart and friendly Pokémon. So much so that there’s a theory that Herdier was the first Pokémon to partner with people.

stoutland.description: These Pokémon seem to enjoy living with humans. Even a Stoutland caught in the wild will warm up to people in about three days.

purrloin.description: It steals things from people just to amuse itself with their frustration. A rivalry exists between this Pokémon and Nickit.

liepard.description: Don’t be fooled by its gorgeous fur and elegant figure. This is a moody and vicious Pokémon.

pansage.description: It’s good at finding berries and gathers them from all over. It’s kind enough to share them with friends.

simisage.description: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.

pansear.description: This Pokémon lives in caves in volcanoes. The fire within the tuft on its head can reach 600 degrees Fahrenheit.

simisear.description: When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.

panpour.description: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.

simipour.description: It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.

munna.description: Late at night, it appears beside people’s pillows. As it feeds on dreams, the patterns on its body give off a faint glow.

musharna.description: When dark mists emanate from its body, don’t get too near. If you do, your nightmares will become reality.

pidove.description: Where people go, these Pokémon follow. If you’re scattering food for them, be careful— several hundred of them can gather at once.

tranquill.description: It can fly moderately quickly. No matter how far it travels, it can always find its way back to its master and its nest.

unfezant.description: Unfezant are exceptional fliers. The females are known for their stamina, while the males outclass them in terms of speed.

blitzle.description: Its heartbeat generates electricity. When Blitzle is surprised and its heart rate goes up, the voltage of its electricity also rises.

zebstrika.description: This Pokémon is aggressive and has a volatile disposition. When agitated, it will illuminate its mane in yellow and fire off bolts of electricity.

roggenrola.description: It’s as hard as steel, but apparently a long soak in water will cause it to soften a bit.

boldore.description: If you see its orange crystals start to glow, be wary. It’s about to fire off bursts of energy.

gigalith.description: This hardy Pokémon can often be found on construction sites and in mines, working alongside people and Copperajah.

woobat.description: While inside a cave, if you look up and see lots of heart-shaped marks lining the walls, it’s evidence that Woobat live there.

swoobat.description: Emitting powerful sound waves tires it out. Afterward, it won’t be able to fly for a little while.

drilbur.description: It can dig through the ground at a speed of 30 mph. It could give a car running aboveground a good race.

excadrill.description: Forming a drill with its steel claws and head, it can bore through a steel plate, no matter how thick it is.

audino.description: Audino’s sense of hearing is superb. Not even a pebble rolling along over a mile away will escape Audino’s ears.

timburr.description: Always carrying squared logs, they help out with construction. As they grow, they carry bigger logs.

gurdurr.description: They strengthen their bodies by carrying steel beams. They show off their big muscles to their friends.

conkeldurr.description: It is thought that Conkeldurr taught humans how to make concrete more than 2,000 years ago.

tympole.description: Graceful ripples running across the water’s surface are a sure sign that Tympole are singing in high-pitched voices below.

palpitoad.description: It weakens its prey with sound waves intense enough to cause headaches, then entangles them with its sticky tongue.

seismitoad.description: The vibrating of the bumps all over its body causes earthquake-like tremors. Seismitoad and Croagunk are similar species.

throh.description: It performs throwing moves with first-rate skill. Over the course of many battles, Throh’s belt grows darker as it absorbs its wearer’s sweat.

sawk.description: If you see a Sawk training in the mountains in its single-minded pursuit of strength, it’s best to quietly pass by.

sewaddle.description: Sewaddle chews on leaves to make its clothing. It’s trying to mimic the leafy garment Leavanny first dressed it in.

swadloon.description: Swadloon lives quietly at the feet of trees. It prefers eating fallen leaves that have grown soft rather than fresh ones.

leavanny.description: This gentle Pokémon has strong protective instincts. The leaves on its arms are sharp enough to slice a thick tree in half with one stroke.

venipede.description: Venipede and Sizzlipede are similar species, but when the two meet, a huge fight ensues.

whirlipede.description: This Pokémon spins itself rapidly and charges into its opponents. Its top speed is just over 60 mph.

scolipede.description: Scolipede latches on to its prey with the claws on its neck before slamming them into the ground and jabbing them with its claws’ toxic spikes.

cottonee.description: Pillows and beds stuffed with cotton exhaled by Cottonee are soft and puffy, light and airy— altogether top quality.

whimsicott.description: Like the wind, it can slip through any gap, no matter how small. It leaves balls of white fluff behind.

petilil.description: The leaves on its head grow right back even if they fall out. These bitter leaves refresh those who eat them.

lilligant.description: The fragrance of the garland on its head has a relaxing effect, but taking care of it is very difficult.

basculin.description: Its temperament is vicious and aggressive. This Pokémon is also full of vitality and can multiply rapidly before anyone notices.

sandile.description: It submerges itself in sand and moves as if swimming. This wise behavior keeps its enemies from finding it and maintains its temperature.

krokorok.description: Protected by thin membranes, their eyes can see even in the dead of night. They live in groups of a few individuals.

krookodile.description: After clamping down with its powerful jaws, it twists its body around to rip its prey in half.

darumaka.description: It derives its power from fire burning inside its body. If the fire dwindles, this Pokémon will immediately fall asleep.

darmanitan.description: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

maractus.description: With noises that could be mistaken for the rattles of maracas, it creates an upbeat rhythm, startling bird Pokémon and making them fly off in a hurry.

dwebble.description: When it finds a stone appealing, it creates a hole inside it and uses it as its home. This Pokémon is the natural enemy of Roggenrola and Rolycoly.

crustle.description: This highly territorial Pokémon prefers dry climates. It won’t come out of its boulder on rainy days.

scraggy.description: It stretches its saggy skin up to its neck to protect itself. Among Scraggy, individuals with saggier skin apparently garner more respect.

scrafty.description: Groups of them beat up anything that enters their territory. Each can spit acidic liquid from its mouth.

sigilyph.description: Psychic power allows these Pokémon to fly. Some say they were the guardians of an ancient city. Others say they were the guardians’ emissaries.

yamask.description: It wanders through ruins by night, carrying a mask that’s said to have been the face it had when it was still human.

cofagrigus.description: This Pokémon has a body of sparkling gold. People say it no longer remembers that it was once human.

tirtouga.description: This Pokémon inhabited ancient seas. Although it can only crawl, it still comes up onto land in search of prey.

carracosta.description: Carracosta completely devours its prey—bones, shells, and all. Because of this, Carracosta’s own shell grows thick and sturdy.

archen.description: This Pokémon was successfully restored from a fossil. As research suggested, Archen is unable to fly. But it’s very good at jumping.

archeops.description: It needs a running start to take off. If Archeops wants to fly, it first needs to run nearly 25 mph, building speed over a course of about 2.5 miles.

trubbish.description: Its favorite places are unsanitary ones. If you leave trash lying around, you could even find one of these Pokémon living in your room.

garbodor.description: This Pokémon eats trash, which turns into poison inside its body. The main component of the poison depends on what sort of trash was eaten.

zorua.description: It changes into the forms of others to surprise them. Apparently, it often transforms into a silent child.

zoroark.description: Stories say those who tried to catch Zoroark were trapped in an illusion and punished.

minccino.description: When its tail has gotten dirty from self-cleaning or from cleaning its nest, Minccino spends a whole day washing its tail in clean springwater.

cinccino.description: Their white fur is coated in a special oil that makes it easy for them to deflect attacks.

gothita.description: This Pokémon is normally very innocent. When it is staring at something invisible, it is unblinking and utterly silent.

gothorita.description: This Pokémon will hypnotize children to put them to sleep before carrying them away. Be wary of nights when the starlight is bright.

gothitelle.description: Gothitelle unleashes psychic energy and shows opponents dreams of the universe’s end. These dreams are apparently ethereal and beautiful.

solosis.description: Because their bodies are enveloped in a special liquid, they can survive in any environment.

duosion.description: Since they have two divided brains, at times they suddenly try to take two different actions at once.

reuniclus.description: Their arms are made of a special liquid. They use psychic power to control these arms and crush boulders.

ducklett.description: It’s not very good at flying yet. It watches the dances of its Swanna parents to learn how to move its wings.

swanna.description: Centered around its leader, the flock dances in perfect sync to strengthen its unity.

vanillite.description: Unable to survive in hot areas, it makes itself comfortable by breathing out air cold enough to cause snow. It burrows into the snow to sleep.

vanillish.description: By drinking pure water, it grows its icy body. This Pokémon can be hard to find on days with warm, sunny weather.

vanilluxe.description: When its anger reaches a breaking point, this Pokémon unleashes a fierce blizzard that freezes every creature around it, be they friend or foe.

deerling.description: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In early spring, these Pokémon give off a delicate, sweet, and calming scent.

sawsbuck.description: It seems that a Sawsbuck with many flowers on its antlers will grow at a slightly slower pace because the flowers absorb the Pokémon’s nutrients.

emolga.description: As Emolga flutters through the air, it crackles with electricity. This Pokémon is cute, but it can cause a lot of trouble.

karrablast.description: Its strange physiology reacts to electrical energy in interesting ways. The presence of a Shelmet will cause this Pokémon to evolve.

escavalier.description: They use shells they’ve stolen from Shelmet to arm and protect themselves. They’re very popular Pokémon in the Galar region.

foongus.description: There is a theory that the developer of the modern-day Poké Ball really liked Foongus, but this has not been confirmed.

amoonguss.description: Be wary of the poisonous spores it releases. Mushrooms resembling Amoonguss’s caps will grow out of anywhere the spores touch.

frillish.description: It envelops its prey in its veillike arms and draws it down to the deeps, five miles below the ocean’s surface.

jellicent.description: Most of this Pokémon’s body composition is identical to sea water. It makes sunken ships its lair.

alomomola.description: It gently holds injured and weak Pokémon in its fins. Its special membrane heals their wounds.

joltik.description: Joltik that live in cities have learned a technique for sucking electricity from the outlets in houses.

galvantula.description: They employ an electrically charged web to trap their prey. While it is immobilized by shock, they leisurely consume it.

ferroseed.description: It defends itself by launching spikes, but its aim isn’t very good at first. Only after a lot of practice will it improve.

ferrothorn.description: This Pokémon scrapes its spikes across rocks, and then uses the tips of its feelers to absorb the nutrients it finds within the stone.

klink.description: The two minigears that compose this Pokémon are closer than twins. They mesh well only with each other.

klang.description: When Klang goes all out, the minigear links up perfectly with the outer part of the big gear, and this Pokémon’s rotation speed increases sharply.

klinklang.description: From its spikes, it launches powerful blasts of electricity. Its red core contains an enormous amount of energy.

tynamo.description: While one alone doesn’t have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.

eelektrik.description: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.

eelektross.description: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

elgyem.description: If this Pokémon stands near a TV, strange scenery will appear on the screen. That scenery is said to be from its home.

beheeyem.description: Whenever a Beheeyem visits a farm, a Dubwool mysteriously disappears.

litwick.description: Its flame is usually out, but it starts shining when Litwick absorbs life-force from people or Pokémon.

lampent.description: Lampent appears at the moment of death and promptly absorbs the spirit as it leaves the body.

chandelure.description: The spirits burned up in its ominous flame lose their way and wander this world forever.

axew.description: This Pokémon lives in nests that are made in the ground. People in ancient times used its tusks as cooking knives.

fraxure.description: Because its tusks don’t grow back once they break, this Pokémon apparently won’t use them unless truly necessary.

haxorus.description: This Pokémon nests in caves and abandoned mines. It is docile, but it will become incredibly angry if its tusks are touched, so beware.

cubchoo.description: Many of this species can be found along the shorelines of cold regions. If a Cubchoo lacks dangling snot, there’s a chance it is sick.

beartic.description: It is a ferocious, carnivorous Pokémon. Once it captures its prey, it will breathe cold air onto the prey to freeze and preserve it.

cryogonal.description: Cryogonal appear during cold seasons. It is said that people and Pokémon who die on snowy mountains are reborn into these Pokémon.

shelmet.description: When attacked, it tightly shuts the lid of its shell. This reaction fails to protect it from Karrablast, however, because they can still get into the shell.

accelgor.description: It moves with blinding speed and lobs poison at foes. Featuring Accelgor as a main character is a surefire way to make a movie or comic popular.

stunfisk.description: Thanks to bacteria that lived in the mud flats with it, this Pokémon developed the organs it uses to generate electricity.

mienfoo.description: In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. With their sharp claws, they cut enemies.

mienshao.description: When Mienshao lets out a bizarre wail, you’re in danger. A flurry of kicks and chops too fast to see is about to be unleashed!

druddigon.description: Druddigon lives in caves, but it never skips sunbathing—it won’t be able to move if its body gets too cold.

golett.description: These Pokémon are thought to have been created by the science of an ancient and mysterious civilization.

golurk.description: When the seal on its chest is removed, it rages indiscriminately. During such rampages, it can turn a whole town into a mountain of rubble.

pawniard.description: Pawniard will fearlessly challenge even powerful foes. In a pinch, it will cling to opponents and pierce them with the blades all over its body.

bisharp.description: This Pokémon commands a group of several Pawniard. Groups that are defeated in territorial disputes are absorbed by the winning side.

bouffalant.description: These Pokémon can crush a car with no more than a headbutt. Bouffalant with more hair on their heads hold higher positions within the herd.

rufflet.description: They pick fights indiscriminately. They grow stronger and more powerful each time they faint or are injured.

braviary.description: The more scars they have, the more respect these brave soldiers of the sky get from their peers.

vullaby.description: They tend to guard their posteriors with suitable bones they have found. They pursue weak Pokémon.

mandibuzz.description: It’s always searching for food for Vullaby. When it finds a weak Pokémon, Mandibuzz swoops it right off to its nest.

heatmor.description: There’s a hole in its tail that allows it to draw in the air it needs to keep its fire burning. If the hole gets blocked, this Pokémon will fall ill.

durant.description: They lay their eggs deep inside their nests. When attacked by Heatmor, they retaliate using their massive mandibles.

deino.description: It can’t see, so its first approach to examining things is to bite them. You will be covered in wounds until a Deino warms up to you.

zweilous.description: The two heads do not get along at all. If you don’t give each head the same amount of attention, they’ll begin fighting out of jealousy.

hydreigon.description: Only the central head has a brain. It is very intelligent, but it thinks only of destruction.

larvesta.description: This Pokémon was called the Larva That Stole the Sun. The fire Larvesta spouts from its horns can cut right through a sheet of iron.

volcarona.description: Its burning body causes it to be unpopular in hot parts of the world, but in cold ones, Volcarona is revered as an embodiment of the sun.

cobalion.description: This Pokémon appears in a legend alongside Terrakion and Virizion, fighting against humans in defense of the Unova region’s Pokémon.

terrakion.description: It has phenomenal power. It will mercilessly crush anyone or anything that bullies small Pokémon.

virizion.description: A legend tells of this Pokémon working together with Cobalion and Terrakion to protect the Pokémon of the Unova region.

tornadus.description: Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

thundurus.description: As it flies around, it shoots lightning all over the place and causes forest fires. It is therefore disliked.

reshiram.description: Flames spew from its tail as it flies through the sky like a jet airplane. It’s said that this Pokémon will scorch the world.

zekrom.description: When the interior part of its tail spins like a motor, Zekrom can generate many bolts of lightning to blast its surroundings.

landorus.description: From the forces of lightning and wind, it creates energy to give nutrients to the soil and make the land abundant.

kyurem.description: Dwelling within it is a power even greater than that of Reshiram or Zekrom, but the extreme cold keeps that power bound.

keldeo.description: Cobalion, Terrakion, and Virizion taught this Pokémon how to fight. It dashes across the world, seeking more opportunities to further its training.

meloetta.description: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.

genesect.description: This Pokémon existed 300 million years ago. Team Plasma altered it and attached a cannon to its back.

basculinbluestriped.description: Its temperament is vicious and aggressive. This Pokémon is also full of vitality and can multiply rapidly before anyone notices.

darmanitanzen.description: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

meloettapirouette.description: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.

tornadustherian.description: Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

thundurustherian.description: As it flies around, it shoots lightning all over the place and causes forest fires. It is therefore disliked.

landorustherian.description: From the forces of lightning and wind, it creates energy to give nutrients to the soil and make the land abundant.

kyuremblack.description: Dwelling within it is a power even greater than that of Reshiram or Zekrom, but the extreme cold keeps that power bound.

kyuremwhite.description: Dwelling within it is a power even greater than that of Reshiram or Zekrom, but the extreme cold keeps that power bound.

keldeoresolute.description: Cobalion, Terrakion, and Virizion taught this Pokémon how to fight. It dashes across the world, seeking more opportunities to further its training.

audinomega.description: Audino’s sense of hearing is superb. Not even a pebble rolling along over a mile away will escape Audino’s ears.

darumakagalar.description: It derives its power from fire burning inside its body. If the fire dwindles, this Pokémon will immediately fall asleep.

darmanitangalar.description: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

darmanitangalarzen.description: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

yamaskgalar.description: It wanders through ruins by night, carrying a mask that’s said to have been the face it had when it was still human.

stunfiskgalar.description: Thanks to bacteria that lived in the mud flats with it, this Pokémon developed the organs it uses to generate electricity.

garbodorgmax.description: This Pokémon eats trash, which turns into poison inside its body. The main component of the poison depends on what sort of trash was eaten.

samurotthisui.description: A master of a sword-drawing art called iaijutsu, Samurott settles its battles with a single swing of either large sword sheathed in its foreleg armor.

lilliganthisui.description: The fragrance of the garland on its head has a relaxing effect, but taking care of it is very difficult.

zoruahisui.description: It changes into the forms of others to surprise them. Apparently, it often transforms into a silent child.

zoroarkhisui.description: Stories say those who tried to catch Zoroark were trapped in an illusion and punished.

braviaryhisui.description: The more scars they have, the more respect these brave soldiers of the sky get from their peers.

basculinwhitestriped.description: Its temperament is vicious and aggressive. This Pokémon is also full of vitality and can multiply rapidly before anyone notices.

darmanitangalarstandard.description: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

emboarmega.description: The flames blazing deep inside Emboar’s chest erupt vigorously from its chin, forming a beard of fire.

excadrillmega.description: Forming a drill with its steel claws and head, it can bore through a steel plate, no matter how thick it is.

scolipedemega.description: Scolipede latches on to its prey with the claws on its neck before slamming them into the ground and jabbing them with its claws’ toxic spikes.

scraftymega.description: Groups of them beat up anything that enters their territory. Each can spit acidic liquid from its mouth.

eelektrossmega.description: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

chandeluremega.description: The spirits burned up in its ominous flame lose their way and wander this world forever.

golurkmega.description: When the seal on its chest is removed, it rages indiscriminately. During such rampages, it can turn a whole town into a mountain of rubble.

chespin.description: When Chespin tenses up just before landing a headbutt, the spikes on its head sharpen to points, piercing the enemy’s body on contact.

quilladin.description: It’s protected by a sturdy shell. The shell is also very heavy, which naturally strengthens Quilladin’s lower body.

chesnaught.description: When its allies are in trouble, Chesnaught creates a shield with its arms and uses its own body to block attacks.

fennekin.description: This Pokémon gets worked up easily. Its body can also overheat, so it uses its ears to dissipate the heat and calm down.

braixen.description: It ignites the twig from its tail and waves the twig around to signal its allies. To indicate danger, it draws circles in the air with the twig’s flame.

delphox.description: It leaves burn marks in the ground with the flame at the tip of its wand. Long ago, people used the shapes of these burn marks for divination.

froakie.description: Its happy-go-lucky look is an act intended to fool its enemies. It will suddenly drop the facade and overwhelm its foes with its blinding speed.

frogadier.description: It excels at devising battle strategies that make use of the terrain, and it never misses its mark when throwing bubble-covered pebbles.

greninja.description: The movement of air against the long tongue Greninja keeps wrapped around its neck allows it to sense enemies it can’t see.

bunnelby.description: It excels at digging holes. Using its ears, it can dig a nest 33 feet deep in one night.

diggersby.description: With power equal to an excavator, it can dig through dense bedrock. It’s a huge help during tunnel construction.

fletchling.description: This Pokémon is normally calm, but once it enters battle, its hormonal balance changes and it becomes aggressive.

fletchinder.description: Fletchinder scatters embers in tall grass where bug Pokémon might be hiding and then catches them as they come leaping out.

talonflame.description: It has top-notch flying capabilities. It flies around easily, even while carrying prey that weighs more than 220 lbs.

scatterbug.description: Any poison this Pokémon takes in is converted into a black powder and secreted. That’s why Scatterbug can eat poisonous leaves and roots.

spewpa.description: If Rufflet attacks this Pokémon by pecking at it, it will retaliate with its sharp fur and poisonous black powder.

vivillon.description: The patterns on this Pokémon depend on the climate and topography of the land it was born in. This form is from frigid lands.

litleo.description: When Litleo are young, female Pyroar will teach them how to hunt. Once the Litleo mature, they will leave the pride and set out on their own.

pyroar.description: The females of a pride work together to bring down prey. It’s thanks to them that their pride doesn’t starve.

flabebe.description: This Pokémon can draw forth the power hidden within blooming wild flowers. It is particularly fond of red flowers.

floette.description: This Pokémon draws forth what power is left in withered flowers to make them healthy again. It holds a red flower.

florges.description: This Pokémon creates an impressive flower garden in its territory. It draws forth the power of the red flowers around its neck.

skiddo.description: Until recently, people living in the mountains would ride on the backs of these Pokémon to traverse the mountain paths.

gogoat.description: It can sense the feelings of others by touching them with its horns. This species has assisted people with their work since 5,000 years ago.

pancham.description: It chooses a Pangoro as its master and then imitates its master’s actions. This is how it learns to battle and hunt for prey.

pangoro.description: This Pokémon is quick to anger, and it has no problem using its prodigious strength to get its way. It lives for duels against Obstagoon.

furfrou.description: There was an era when aristocrats would compete to see who could trim their Furfrou’s fur into the most exquisite style.

espurr.description: It keeps its ears covered to prevent the intense psychic power in its body from escaping, but it falls unconscious if this power builds too much.

meowstic.description: Though it has enough psychic power to blast away any opponent, Meowstic prefers to support its allies rather than attack.

honedge.description: Honedge’s soul once belonged to a person who was killed a long time ago by the sword that makes up Honedge’s body.

doublade.description: Honedge evolves into twins. The two blades rub together to emit a metallic sound that unnerves opponents.

aegislash.description: In this defensive stance, Aegislash uses its steel body and a force field of spectral power to reduce the damage of any attack.

spritzee.description: A scent pouch within this Pokémon’s body allows it to create various scents. A change in its diet will alter the fragrance it produces.

aromatisse.description: The scent that constantly emits from its fur is so powerful that this Pokémon’s companions will eventually lose their sense of smell.

swirlix.description: It eats its own weight in sugar every day. If it doesn’t get enough sugar, it becomes incredibly grumpy.

slurpuff.description: By taking in a person’s scent, it can sniff out their mental and physical condition. It’s hoped that this skill will have many medical applications.

inkay.description: It protects itself from tough foes by flashing its luminescent spots to discourage them.

malamar.description: Its hypnotic powers are dangerously strong. Anyone who falls under Malamar’s control loses their memories surrounding the event.

binacle.description: After two Binacle find a suitably sized rock, they adhere themselves to it and live together. They cooperate to gather food during high tide.

barbaracle.description: Seven Binacle come together to form one Barbaracle. The Binacle that serves as the head gives orders to those serving as the limbs.

skrelp.description: Skrelp evades its enemies by hiding amid drifting seaweed. It eats rotten seaweed to create its poison.

dragalge.description: Using a liquid poison, Dragalge indiscriminately attacks anything that wanders into its territory. This poison can corrode the undersides of boats.

clauncher.description: This Pokémon launches water by detonating gas inside its right claw. It snipes flying Pokémon.

clawitzer.description: Clawitzer can move through the water at a speed of 60 knots by using gas inside its body to expel water from the back of its claw.

helioptile.description: When spread, the frills on its head act like solar panels, generating the power behind this Pokémon’s electric moves.

heliolisk.description: A now-vanished desert culture treasured these Pokémon. Appropriately, when Heliolisk came to the Galar region, treasure came with them.

tyrunt.description: This is an ancient Pokémon, revived in modern times. It has a violent disposition, and it’ll tear apart anything it gets between its hefty jaws.

tyrantrum.description: This Pokémon is from about 100,000,000 years ago. It has the presence of a king, vicious but magnificent.

amaura.description: This Pokémon was successfully restored from a fossil. In the past, it lived with others of its kind in cold lands where there were fewer predators.

aurorus.description: Aurorus was restored from a fossil. It’s said that when this Pokémon howls, auroras appear in the night sky.

sylveon.description: This Pokémon uses its ribbonlike feelers to send a soothing aura into its opponents, erasing their hostility.

hawlucha.description: Its elegant finishing moves—performed by nimbly leaping around using its wings—are polished in the forest where it was born and raised.

dedenne.description: It’s small and its electricity-generating organ is not fully developed, so it uses its tail to absorb electricity from people’s homes and charge itself.

carbink.description: It has slept underground for hundreds of millions of years since its birth. It’s occasionally found during the excavation of caves.

goomy.description: Most of a Goomy’s body is water. A membrane covers the whole Pokémon to prevent it from shriveling up in dry weather.

sliggoo.description: The swirly protrusion on its back is filled with all its vital organs, such as its brain and heart.

goodra.description: It loves the rain. This mellow Pokémon can be seen walking around on the plains and in the mountains on rainy days.

klefki.description: Once it absorbs a key’s metal ions, it discards the key without a second thought. However, it will hang on to keys it favors for decades.

phantump.description: Legend tells that its green leaves can cure any illness. When plucked, however, the leaves will instantly wither away.

trevenant.description: Using its roots, Trevenant connects itself to trees and monitors every corner of its forest. It uses curses to drive intruders away.

pumpkaboo.description: Spirits that wander this world are placed into Pumpkaboo’s body. They’re then moved on to the afterlife.

gourgeist.description: Eerie cries emanate from its body in the dead of night. The sounds are said to be the wails of spirits who are suffering in the afterlife.

bergmite.description: They live in mountainous regions of frigid cold. On rare occasions, they ride on the back of an Avalugg to cross seas and move to new habitats.

avalugg.description: As Avalugg walks along with Bergmite on its back, it comes across pods of Cetitan. It lets them pass to avoid conflict.

noibat.description: This Pokémon emits ultrasonic waves from its large ears to search for fruit to eat. It mistakes Applin for its food.

noivern.description: Ultrasonic waves emitted by a Noivern can pulverize a large boulder. This Pokémon has a cruel disposition.

xerneas.description: When the horns on its head shine in seven colors, it is said to be sharing everlasting life.

yveltal.description: When its life comes to an end, it absorbs the life energy of every living thing and turns into a cocoon once more.

zygarde.description: This is Zygarde’s form when about half of its pieces have been assembled. It plays the role of monitoring the ecosystem.

diancie.description: It can instantly create many diamonds by compressing the carbon in the air between its hands.

hoopa.description: It is said to be able to seize anything it desires with its six rings and six huge arms. With its power sealed, it is transformed into a much smaller form.

volcanion.description: It expels its internal steam from the arms on its back. It has enough power to blow away a mountain.

rowlet.description: Silently it glides, streaking toward its targets to get close to them. Before they even notice it, it begins to pelt them with vicious kicks.

dartrix.description: This narcissistic Pokémon is a clean freak. If you don’t groom it diligently, it may stop listening to you.

decidueye.description: It cunningly conceals arrow quills in its wings. It launches these quills with such precision that they can pierce a pebble at over a hundred yards.

litten.description: If you try too hard to get close to it, it won’t open up to you. Even if you do grow close, giving it too much affection is still a no-no.

torracat.description: At its throat, it bears a bell of fire. The bell rings brightly whenever fire spews out.

incineroar.description: When its fighting spirit is set alight, the flames around its waist become especially intense.

popplio.description: This Pokémon can control balloons made of water. It practices diligently so it can learn to make big balloons.

brionne.description: A skillful dancer, it creates a sequence of water balloons as it dances, then briskly bombards its enemies.

primarina.description: To Primarina, every battle is a stage. It takes down its prey with beautiful singing and dancing.

pikipek.description: Using its beak to strike 16 times per second, it opens holes in even the hardest of trees.

trumbeak.description: It flies around using a hundred different cries in various ways to declare its territory to others.

toucannon.description: The compressed gas in Toucannon’s beak launches seeds with such force that they can shatter large boulders.

yungoos.description: Its stomach fills most of its torso. It wanders the same path every day, searching for fresh food.

gumshoos.description: Once it finds signs of prey, it will patiently stake out the location, waiting until the sun goes down.

grubbin.description: Grubbin normally live underground, but if they get unearthed by Hoothoot, they may be found gathered around electric Pokémon.

charjabug.description: Protected by a sturdy shell, Charjabug eats large quantities of fresh and decomposing leaf litter in order to evolve.

vikavolt.description: Displaying exceptional mobility, it weaves between trees and shoots down bird Pokémon with its electromagnetic beams.

crabrawler.description: This Pokémon punches trees and eats the berries that drop down, training itself and getting food at the same time.

crabominable.description: The detached pincers of these Pokémon are delicious. Some Trainers bring Lechonk into the mountains just to search for them.

oricorio.description: This Pokémon is incredibly popular, possibly because its passionate dancing is a great match with the temperament of Paldean people.

cutiefly.description: When it senses the auras of people or Pokémon who are having fun, it will draw close and give them a painful poke with its long proboscis.

ribombee.description: Ribombee can sense when people or Pokémon are feeling down, and it will cheer them up with handmade pollen puffs.

rockruff.description: This Pokémon is very friendly when it’s young. Its disposition becomes vicious once it matures, but it never forgets the kindness of its master.

lycanroc.description: Lycanroc attacks its prey with its sharp claws and fangs. It loyally obeys the instructions of a Trainer it trusts.

wishiwashi.description: Individually, they’re incredibly weak. It’s by gathering up into schools that they’re able to confront opponents.

mareanie.description: This Pokémon wanders the seaside looking for food. It often gets electric shocks from broken Pincurchin spines that it tries to eat.

toxapex.description: This Pokémon lives within a dome made by its own legs. Toxapex monitors its surroundings by sensing the flow of the tide through its spikes.

mudbray.description: This Pokémon covers itself in mud that it has regurgitated. The mud won’t dry out even if it’s exposed to the sun for a long time.

mudsdale.description: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.

dewpider.description: Dewpider uses sticky threads to create the water bubble that covers its head, so the bubble very rarely bursts.

araquanid.description: A caring Pokémon, Araquanid carries Dewpider around inside its water bubble to protect them as it walks. It protects its food in its bubble too.

fomantis.description: Fomantis hates having its naps interrupted. It fires off beams using energy it gathers by bathing in the sun.

lurantis.description: By masquerading as a bug Pokémon, it lowers the guard of actual bug Pokémon lured in by a scent of sweet flowers. Its sickles bring them down.

morelull.description: Pokémon living in the forest eat the delicious caps on Morelull’s head. The caps regrow overnight.

shiinotic.description: Its flickering spores lure in prey and put them to sleep. Once this Pokémon has its prey snoozing, it drains their vitality with its fingertips.

salandit.description: It taunts its prey and lures them into narrow, rocky areas where it then sprays them with toxic gas to make them dizzy and take them down.

salazzle.description: Salazzle makes its opponents light-headed with poisonous gas, then captivates them with alluring movements to turn them into loyal servants.

stufful.description: Its fluffy fur is a delight to pet, but carelessly reaching out to touch this Pokémon could result in painful retaliation.

bewear.description: Once it accepts you as a friend, it tries to show its affection with a hug. Letting it do that is dangerous—it could easily shatter your bones.

bounsweet.description: Its sweat is sweet, like syrup made from boiled- down fruit. Because of this, Bounsweet was highly valued in the past, when sweeteners were scarce.

steenee.description: Steenee spreads a sweet scent that makes others feel invigorated. This same scent is popular for antiperspirants.

tsareena.description: This Pokémon is proud and aggressive. However, it is said that a Tsareena will instantly become calm if someone touches the crown on its calyx.

comfey.description: It uses its vine to pick flowers. The flowers that Comfey attaches to itself develop healing properties.

oranguru.description: People used to mistake Oranguru for a human when they saw it issue command after command to the other Pokémon of the forest.

passimian.description: This Pokémon battles by throwing hard berries. It won’t obey a Trainer who throws Poké Balls without skill.

wimpod.description: It’s nature’s cleaner—it eats anything and everything, including garbage and rotten things. The ground near its nest is always clean.

golisopod.description: It will do anything to win, taking advantage of every opening and finishing opponents off with the small claws on its front legs.

sandygast.description: If it loses its shovel, it will stick something else— like a branch—in its head to make do until it finds another shovel.

palossand.description: The terrifying Palossand drags smaller Pokémon into its sandy body. Once its victims are trapped, it drains them of their vitality whenever it pleases.

pyukumuku.description: It lives in warm, shallow waters. If it encounters a foe, it will spit out its internal organs as a means to punch them.

typenull.description: Rumor has it that the theft of top-secret research notes led to a new instance of this Pokémon being created in the Galar region.

minior.description: This Pokémon is born in the ozone layer. It falls to the ground once the outer shell enclosing its core grows heavy.

komala.description: Komala spends its entire life sleeping. It feeds on leaves that contain a potent poison only Komala can break down.

turtonator.description: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.

togedemaru.description: With the long hairs on its back, this Pokémon takes in electricity from other electric Pokémon. It stores what it absorbs in an electric sac.

mimikyu.description: This Pokémon lives in dark places untouched by sunlight. When it appears before humans, it hides itself under a cloth that resembles a Pikachu.

bruxish.description: It grinds its teeth with great force to stimulate its brain. It fires the psychic energy created by this process from the protuberance on its head.

drampa.description: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.

dhelmise.description: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.

jangmoo.description: The scale atop its head is useful for both offense and defense. It bravely stands and faces its foes rather than turning tail, even if its foes are strong.

hakamoo.description: It gets into fistfights so intense that the scales on its arms peel off. Bare arms are a sign of valiance.

kommoo.description: It lets its arm hang, and then—quick as a flash— swings upward to land its specialty punch and send the opponent flying high into the sky.

tapukoko.description: Although it’s called a guardian deity, if a person or Pokémon puts it in a bad mood, it will become a malevolent deity and attack.

tapulele.description: It heals the wounds of people and Pokémon by sprinkling them with its sparkling scales. This guardian deity is worshiped on Akala.

tapubulu.description: Although it’s called a guardian deity, it’s violent enough to crush anyone it sees as an enemy.

tapufini.description: This guardian deity of Poni Island manipulates water. Because it lives deep within a thick fog, it came to be both feared and revered.

cosmog.description: This Pokémon came from another universe. Its gaseous body is so light that even a gentle breeze can blow it away.

cosmoem.description: The absorption of starlight fuels this Pokémon’s growth. The shell that encases it is harder than any known material.

solgaleo.description: When light radiates from its body, this Pokémon could almost appear to be the sun. It will dispel any darkness and light up the world.

lunala.description: Known as the Beast That Calls the Moon, this Pokémon lives by taking in any and all light and converting it into its own energy.

nihilego.description: A life-form from another world, it was dubbed a UB and is thought to produce a strong neurotoxin.

buzzwole.description: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

pheromosa.description: A life-form that lives in another world, its body is thin and supple, but it also possesses great power.

xurkitree.description: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

celesteela.description: One of the dangerous UBs, high energy readings can be detected coming from both of its huge arms.

kartana.description: This Ultra Beast’s body, which is as thin as paper, is like a sharpened sword.

guzzlord.description: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

necrozma.description: It survives by absorbing light. After a long time spent slumbering underground, impurities accumulated within it, causing its body to darken.

magearna.description: It synchronizes its consciousness with others to understand their feelings. This faculty makes it useful for taking care of people.

marshadow.description: By slipping into the shadow of a martial arts master and copying their movements, this Pokémon learned the ultimate techniques.

poipole.description: This Ultra Beast is well enough liked to be chosen as a first partner in its own world.

naganadel.description: It stores hundreds of liters of poisonous liquid inside its body. It is one of the organisms known as UBs.

stakataka.description: It appeared from an Ultra Wormhole. Each one appears to be made up of many life-forms stacked one on top of each other.

blacephalon.description: It slithers toward people. Then, without warning, it triggers the explosion of its own head. It’s apparently one kind of Ultra Beast.

zeraora.description: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.

meltan.description: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.

melmetal.description: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.

gumshoostotem.description: Once it finds signs of prey, it will patiently stake out the location, waiting until the sun goes down.

vikavolttotem.description: Displaying exceptional mobility, it weaves between trees and shoots down bird Pokémon with its electromagnetic beams.

oricoriopompom.description: This Pokémon is incredibly popular, possibly because its passionate dancing is a great match with the temperament of Paldean people.

wishiwashischool.description: Individually, they’re incredibly weak. It’s by gathering up into schools that they’re able to confront opponents.

lurantistotem.description: By masquerading as a bug Pokémon, it lowers the guard of actual bug Pokémon lured in by a scent of sweet flowers. Its sickles bring them down.

salazzletotem.description: Salazzle makes its opponents light-headed with poisonous gas, then captivates them with alluring movements to turn them into loyal servants.

thwackey.description: It skillfully uses its two sticks not only for drumming out rapid beats but also for pummeling opponents during battle.

rillaboom.description: Though it has a calm disposition, it won’t tolerate those who drum up discord. It strictly disciplines offenders until they learn their lesson.

scorbunny.description: Once its body has heated up, Scorbunny can use the full extent of its power. That’s why it does warm-up exercises.

raboot.description: Thanks to its soft and fluffy fur, Raboot can easily heat up its fire energy and produce flames with more power.

cinderace.description: Although Cinderace loses its cool easily, it will battle flawlessly for a Trainer it trusts.

sobble.description: It gets berries to eat by shooting them down with bullets of water it spurts from its mouth. Its aim is perfect.

drizzile.description: It extends its long, slimy tongue at blinding speeds and finishes off its prey with great skill.

inteleon.description: It uses special lenses in its eyes to sense things about its opponents—like their body heat—then attacks once it identifies a weak spot.

skwovet.description: It stores berries in its cheeks. When there are no berries to be found, Skwovet will stuff pebbles into its cheeks to stave off its cravings.

greedent.description: If it spots a berry tree, it will immediately go to gather berries without a sideways glance—even if it’s in the middle of a battle.

rookidee.description: This Pokémon is brave and reckless. The white markings around a Rookidee’s eyes intimidate fainthearted Pokémon.

corvisquire.description: It’s said that the reason behind Corvisquire’s high level of intelligence is the large size of its brain relative to those of other bird Pokémon.

corviknight.description: Corviknight can’t serve as a taxi service in Paldea because the Pokémon’s natural predators will attack it while it flies, endangering the customer.

blipbug.description: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn’t.

dottler.description: It barely moves, but it’s still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.

orbeetle.description: It’s famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.

nickit.description: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.

thievul.description: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.

gossifleur.description: It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly.

eldegoss.description: The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them.

wooloo.description: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.

dubwool.description: Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You’ll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it.

chewtle.description: Its large front tooth is still growing in. When the tooth itches, this Pokémon will bite another Chewtle’s horn, and the two Pokémon will tussle.

drednaw.description: Its massive, jagged teeth can crush a boulder in a single bite. This Pokémon has an extremely vicious disposition.

yamper.description: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

boltund.description: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

rolycoly.description: On sunny days, Rolycoly will come out onto grassy plains and roll around. Then it will eat the grass that gets tangled in its wheel-like leg.

carkol.description: The temperature inside its body increases when it experiences strong emotions. It rolls around frantically while spewing flames.

coalossal.description: To intimidate its opponents, Coalossal will vigorously shake its body, scattering coal from its smoldering back.

applin.description: It grows by eating the flesh of an apple. Applin uses its own body fluid to strengthen the apple’s skin and prevent it from rotting.

flapple.description: It flutters around while seeking an opening in the opponent’s guard, then attacks by spitting acidic liquid strong enough to melt metal.

appletun.description: It feeds mainly on sweet apples. It will also eat small bug Pokémon that are attracted by its sweet nectar.

silicobra.description: Silicobra’s neck pouch, which can inflate and deflate like a balloon, gets more elastic each time Silicobra sheds its skin.

sandaconda.description: It will expand its body as much as it can and then contract itself, blasting out sand with enough force to wash away a dump truck.

cramorant.description: Cramorant instinctively swallow everything whole. They’re at their most formidable when they’re struggling to swallow overly large prey.

arrokuda.description: Arrokuda can swim quickly only in a straight line. The ones that become sluggish from overeating are the first to be targeted by flocks of Wattrel.

barraskewda.description: It spins its tail fins to leap from the water, then viciously bites down on Wingull flying close to the water’s surface.

toxel.description: It has no problem drinking dirty water. An organ inside Toxel’s body filters such water into a poisonous liquid that is harmless to Toxel.

toxtricity.description: As it scatters toxic sweat and emits electricity, a melody that sounds like it came from a guitar reverberates through the surrounding area.

sizzlipede.description: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

centiskorch.description: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

clobbopus.description: It’s very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.

grapploct.description: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.

sinistea.description: The soul of someone who died alone possessed some leftover tea. This Pokémon appears in hotels and houses.

polteageist.description: The tea that composes Polteageist’s body has a distinct and enjoyable flavor. Drinking too much, however, can be fatal.

hatenna.description: Because the emotions of others constantly flow into its head, this Pokémon prefers environments where no other creatures live.

hattrem.description: To this Pokémon, strong emotions apparently feel like incredibly loud noises—even if the emotions are happy ones.

hatterene.description: Hatterene knocks out those that intrude in its home forest by blasting them with a beam, then slashing with claws enhanced by psychic power.

impidimp.description: The reason this Pokémon causes trouble for those it feels close to is because Impidimp itself gets irritable if it can’t absorb negative emotions.

morgrem.description: Morgrem prefers dirty tactics, like ambushing, because it doesn’t have confidence in its brawn.

grimmsnarl.description: This Pokémon has complete control over its hair. Grimmsnarl normally keeps its hair wrapped around its body to support its muscles.

obstagoon.description: Its voice is staggering in volume. Obstagoon has a tendency to take on a threatening posture and shout—this move is known as Obstruct.

perrserker.description: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.

cursola.description: Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon’s core spirit.

sirfetchd.description: Only Farfetch’d that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon’s leek withers, it will retire from combat.

mrrime.description: It’s highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.

runerigus.description: A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move.

milcery.description: The more sweet aromas it absorbs, the more its body swells. Milcery will deflate when its energy level drops.

alcremie.description: Desserts that Alcremie have decorated with their cream have a rich, sweet flavor and bring happiness to all who eat them.

falinks.description: The brass, which is the one that stands at the front and issues orders, is the strongest and smartest of the six.

pincurchin.description: This Pokémon generates electricity when it digests food. It uses its five hard teeth to scrape seaweed off surfaces and eat it.

snom.description: It eats snow that has accumulated on the ground. It prefers soft, freshly fallen snow, so it will eat its way up a mountain, aiming for the peak.

frosmoth.description: Frosmoth senses air currents with its antennae. It sends its scales drifting on frigid air, making them fall like snow.

stonjourner.description: The elemental composition of the rocks that form its body were found to match the bedrock of a land far away from this Pokémon’s habitat.

eiscue.description: On hot days, these Pokémon press their ice cube heads together and pass the time cooling each other down.

indeedee.description: This Pokémon picks up on the positive emotions of other creatures via its horns and uses those emotions to fuel itself.

morpeko.description: Morpeko eats seeds constantly to keep its hunger at bay. If it’s hungry for too long, it grows wild and brutish.

cufant.description: Using the pointy tip of its trunk, it carves off chunks of hard rocks to eat. It is very docile and helps people with physical labor.

copperajah.description: This Pokémon was brought to Paldea long ago by people from a faraway land. It’s so strong that it can easily pull an airplane.

dracozolt.description: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.

arctozolt.description: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.

dracovish.description: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.

arctovish.description: Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.

duraludon.description: Duraludon’s body is comprised of a special metal that’s lightweight and scratch resistant. It’s also smooth, as though it was given a mirror finish.

dreepy.description: In the evening, groups of Dreepy will fly at high speeds over the ocean and poke at Pokémon in the water for fun.

drakloak.description: This Pokémon flies around at over 120 miles per hour. If a Drakloak is defeated in a battle, its Dreepy will wander off without a second thought.

dragapult.description: Dragapult can make its whole body transparent by clearing its mind and focusing. Even the Dreepy in Dragapult’s horns become invisible.

zacian.description: Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.

zamazenta.description: In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.

eternatus.description: The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.

kubfu.description: Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves.

urshifu.description: This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist.

zarude.description: Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it.

regieleki.description: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power.

regidrago.description: An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.

glastrier.description: Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.

spectrier.description: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body.

calyrex.description: Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore.

wyrdeer.description: Parts of its body turned to stone when it evolved thanks to an extremely rare ore found in volcanic areas.

kleavor.description: This Pokémon is cloaked in the souls of its comrades who perished during a punishing journey to the river of their birth.

ursaluna.description: Overqwil’s poisonous spikes will reflexively react even while Overqwil sleeps, stabbing any moving thing that approaches.

basculegion.description: Its fluffy fur is similar in composition to plants. This Pokémon frequently washes its face to keep it from drying out.

sneasler.description: Floragato deftly wields the vine hidden beneath its long fur, slamming the hard flower bud against its opponents.

overqwil.description: This Pokémon uses the reflective fur lining its cape to camouflage the stem of its flower, creating the illusion that the flower is floating.

enamorus.description: It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.
